heading: Liji 22 · Ji Tong 祭統 · A Summary Account Of Sacrifices · Ji Tong 7 … Ji Tong 11

items.text: Perform your part in the ancestral sacrifice: offer the libation, prepare the offerings, and lead the dance to give pleasure to the personator.
items.quote: The ruler from his mace-handled libation-cup poured out the fragrant spirit before the personator of the dead
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with God's exclusive worship (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Perform your part in the ancestral sacrifice: present the purified liquid and put the offerings on the dishes.
items.quote: his wife put them on the dishes and presented them
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with God's exclusive worship (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Let your blessings flow down to those below you; do not hoard while they are in want.
items.quote: there was no such thing as the superior's accumulating a great amount for himself, while the people below him might be suffering from cold and want

heading: Liji 22 · Ji Tong 祭統 · A Summary Account Of Sacrifices · Ji Tong 28 … Ji Tong 29

items.text: Carry on and out the services of your father.
items.quote: Carry on and out the services of your father.
items.conflict: Worship is due to God alone; the dead cannot hear or help (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Do not praise ancestors for good qualities they did not possess.
items.quote: praised their ancestors for good qualities which they did not possess, that was falsehood

items.text: Take knowledge of the good qualities your ancestors did possess.
items.quote: did not take knowledge of the good qualities which they did possess, that showed their want of intelligence

items.text: Transmit by inscription the good qualities you know of your ancestors.
items.quote: knew them and did not transmit them (by their inscriptions), that showed a want of virtue

heading: Liji 22 · Ji Tong 祭統 · A Summary Account Of Sacrifices · Ji Tong 21 … Ji Tong 27

items.text: In sacrificial rows, take places according to age, so that the old and young are in order.
items.quote: The members of each row had places according to their age; and in the same way were arranged all the assistants at the service.

items.text: At the close of the sacrifice, bestow what is left on the lowest of your servants.
items.quote: when the most honoured, at the close of the sacrifice, did not forget those who were the most mean, but took what was left and bestowed it on them

items.text: In distributing portions at sacrifices, show impartiality: give to the noble and the lowly alike, not too much to one and nothing to another.
items.quote: the nobler did not receive very much, and the lower were not left without any:--impartiality was thus shown

items.text: Preside at the ancestral sacrifice in person, and if you entrust it to another, still understand its meaning.
items.quote: the superior man, when he has a sacrifice, will feel it necessary to preside at it in person... he may commit the performance of it to another
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with Scripture: worship belongs to God alone (Exodus 20:3-5); the dead cannot receive offerings.

items.text: Do not be irreverent in the sacrifices.
items.quote: none of the sons and grandsons within its borders will dare to be irreverent
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with Scripture: worship belongs to God alone (Exodus 20:3-5); the dead cannot receive offerings.

items.text: In inscriptions on sacrificial vessels, mention only the good qualities of your ancestors, not their bad.
items.quote: the idea of an inscription is to make mention of the good qualifies and not of the bad:--such is the heart of a filial descendant

items.text: In celebrating your ancestors, exalt your filial piety.
items.quote: In the celebration of his ancestors he exalts his filial piety

heading: Liji 22 · Ji Tong 祭統 · A Summary Account Of Sacrifices · Ji Tong 1 … Ji Tong 6

items.text: Nourish your parents while they live, showing natural obedience.
items.quote: while they are alive, by nourishing them

items.text: When your parents die, perform all the rites of mourning, showing your sorrow.
items.quote: when they are dead, by all the rites of mourning

items.text: When the mourning is over, sacrifice to your parents, showing reverence and observing the seasons.
items.quote: when the mourning is over by sacrificing to them
items.conflict: Offering sacrifices to the dead conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Assist in the service of the ancestral temple and the altars, as your husband sought you for this purpose.
items.quote: to do service in the ancestral temple, and at the altars to (the spirits of) the land and grain
items.conflict: Assisting in sacrifices to ancestors conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Each spouse must personally attend to his or her own duties in the sacrifices.
items.quote: husband and wife had their several duties which they personally attended to
items.conflict: Personal participation in sacrifices to ancestors conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Personally plough or otherwise labor to provide grain for the sacrificial vessels, showing sincerity.
items.quote: the son of Heaven himself guided the plough in the southern suburb, to provide the grain for the sacrificial vessels
items.conflict: Providing offerings for sacrifices to ancestors conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Personally tend silkworms or otherwise labor to provide silk for the sacrificial robes, showing sincerity.
items.quote: the queen looked after her silkworms in the northern suburb, to provide the cap and robes of silk
items.conflict: Providing offerings for sacrifices to ancestors conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Before offering sacrifice, devote yourself to purification, keeping your thoughts uniform and your conduct proper for seven days and three days.
items.quote: he guarded against all things of an evil nature, and suppressed all his desires
items.conflict: Purification for communion with the dead conflicts with the biblical teaching that only God is to be worshiped and that the dead are not to be contacted (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Offer the sacrifices with all sincerity, good faith, right-heartedness, and reverence, without seeking anything for yourself.
items.quote: he brings into exercise all sincerity and good faith, with all right-heartedness and reverence... without seeking for anything to be gained
items.conflict: Offering sacrifices to the dead conflicts with worship of God alone and with the prohibition of communing with the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

heading: Liji 22 · Ji Tong 祭統 · A Summary Account Of Sacrifices · Ji Tong 12 … Ji Tong 20

items.text: Show filial piety toward your parents.
items.quote: filial piety towards parents

items.text: Serve your father as a son should, with reverence and obedience.
items.quote: how it is the way of a son to serve his father

items.text: Observe the proper order of near and distant, older and younger, without confusion.
items.quote: the distinction was maintained between the order of fathers and sons, the near and the distant, the older and the younger

items.text: Maintain the proper distinction between husband and wife in all mutual giving and receiving.
items.quote: when husband and wife were giving and receiving, the one did not touch the place where the other had held the article

items.text: Reverently sacrifice to the ancestors in the ancestral temple.
items.quote: reverently sacrificed in his ancestral temple
items.conflict: Worship belongs to God alone; offering sacrifice to ancestors is idolatry.

items.text: Yield to elders in the order of drinking, according to age.
items.quote: the cup passed from one to another, according to age

items.text: When you receive an appointment or honor, present it in your ancestral temple.
items.quote: received the writing, returned (home), and presented it in his (own) ancestral temple
items.conflict: Worship belongs to God alone; offering sacrifice to ancestors is idolatry.

items.text: Act as the representative of your grandfather in the sacrifice.
items.quote: a grandson acted as the representative of his grandfather
items.conflict: Worship belongs to God alone; offering sacrifice to ancestors is idolatry.
